brief: Goldman's CTA model puts US 10-year Treasury positioning at roughly 99% of maximum short, and its funds positioning indicator shows an extreme duration underweight, a setup that has historically preceded lower 10-year yields over the following three months. CTAs also hold extreme upside convexity in bonds, so a rally in Treasuries could trigger further systematic buying. Separately, utilities were the most heavily shorted US sector last week (the largest Goldman-tracked utility short selling in almost six years), and JPMorgan's prime-brokerage data shows hedge-fund utility exposure at its lowest since 2018, about 2.5 standard deviations below normal. From September 4 to 25 the 10-year yield rose 39bp while XLU fell about 8.4% relative to SPY, continuing a pattern seen through spring and summer. BofA estimates its Treasury trend position holds unless the 10-year falls roughly 18bp in a week. The note argues that if yields break lower and utilities start outperforming, the two crowded shorts could unwind together, giving the bond rally an equity leg; falling yields without relative utility strength would weaken the thesis.
